title: Boss: the shortener's launch review
summary: A load-test report and a capacity sheet for short.example.com land in your design review. Find the last safe stage, explain the database surge, check five years of storage and pick the code length.

steps.title: The artefact: a load-test report
body: The team ran a stepped load test against the new redirect tier (constant arrival rate, `wrk2 -R`, 10 minutes per
stage). Their SLO: **p99 at most 250 ms and at most 0.1% errors**. The report, as attached to the review:
stage  rps    p50_ms p99_ms errors cache_hit
The capacity sheet asks for 100 M new links a month, kept 5 years, about 500 bytes each, 3 copies.
Reviewers do not eyeball tables like this: they compute. Each step below is one question the review asks.
Notice the cache hit rate falling as load rises: the cache is evicting the hot set (it was sized for stage 2),
so the database takes far more reads at exactly the moment traffic peaks.

steps.title: The last stage that met the SLO
prompt: Write `int LastPassingStage(string[] report, int maxP99Ms, double maxErrors)`.
- `report[0]` is the header; each other line is `stage rps p50_ms p99_ms errors cache_hit`, separated by one or
- Walk the stages in order. Return the number of the last stage before the first one that breaks the SLO
(`p99 > maxP99Ms` or `errors > maxErrors`). If stage 1 already breaks it, return `0`; if none do, return the
starter: int LastPassingStage(string[] report, int maxP99Ms, double maxErrors)
solution: int LastPassingStage(string[] report, int maxP99Ms, double maxErrors)
hints: `line.Split(' ', StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries)` copes with the extra spaces.
p99 is column 3 and errors column 4 (counting from 0). Stop at the first failure.
template: Dojo.Eq("the team's SLO: stage 2 is the last safe one", 2, LastPassingStage(dojoReport, 250, 0.001));
Dojo.Eq("a looser SLO passes stage 3", 3, LastPassingStage(dojoReport, 500, 0.05));
Dojo.Eq("every stage passes a very loose SLO", 4, LastPassingStage(dojoReport, 5000, 0.5));
Dojo.Eq("stage 1 already fails a 10 ms p99", 0, LastPassingStage(dojoReport, 10, 0.0));
Dojo.Eq("a later pass does not count after a failure", 1, LastPassingStage(new[] { "h", "1 1 1 10 0", "2 1 1 900 0", "3 1 1 10 0" }, 100, 0.0));

steps.title: Why the database surged
prompt: Write `long DbReadsPerSecond(long rps, double cacheHit)`: the reads that miss the cache and reach the database,
rounded to the nearest whole number. A hit rate below `0` or above `1` throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`.
Run it on the report: going from stage 2 to stage 3 doubles the traffic but multiplies database reads by 14.5.
hints: `(long)Math.Round(...)` rounds to the nearest whole number.
template: Dojo.Throws<ArgumentOutOfRangeException>("a hit rate above 1 is a bug", () => DbReadsPerSecond(10, 1.5));

steps.title: Five years of storage
prompt: Write `double StorageTb(long linksPerMonth, int bytesPerLink, int years, int copies)`: the total stored after
`years`, in decimal terabytes (1 TB = 10^12 bytes), counting every copy.
The capacity sheet's numbers give 9 TB.
starter: double StorageTb(long linksPerMonth, int bytesPerLink, int years, int copies)
solution: double StorageTb(long linksPerMonth, int bytesPerLink, int years, int copies)
hints: Links = per month x 12 x years. Multiply in `double` to avoid overflow.
Then x bytes x copies, divided by `1e12`.
template: Dojo.Eq("no overflow at large scale", 1080.0, Math.Round(StorageTb(3_000_000_000, 1000, 10, 3), 2));

steps.title: How long must the codes be?
prompt: Write `int CodeLength(long totalLinks, double maxFill)`: the smallest number of base62 characters `L` (at least 1)
such that `totalLinks <= 62^L x maxFill`. `maxFill` is how full the keyspace may get: `0.01` means at most 1% of
possible codes are in use, so a random guess finds a real link about 1 time in 100. A `maxFill` of `0` or less, or
For 6 billion links (5 years at 100 M a month), a 1% fill needs 7 characters and a 0.1% fill needs 8.
hints: Start at 1 and grow while the keyspace times `maxFill` is still smaller than `totalLinks`.
`Math.Pow(62, length)` is exact for these sizes.
template: Dojo.Eq("6 B links at 1% fill", 7, CodeLength(6_000_000_000, 0.01));
Dojo.Eq("6 B links at 0.1% fill", 8, CodeLength(6_000_000_000, 0.001));
